mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals tighter monetary conditions, which may lead to decreased borrowing and spending, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 do not exceed the baseline returns in more than 50% of cases when UNRATE is below 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of cases when HOUST is high, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) growth below 0.5% per month indicates reduced supply-side activity, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO growth is below 0.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is low and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is high, it indicates a potential mismatch in monetary policy, leading to increased market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE is below 4.5% and FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) grows but real federal spending (RSAFS) slows, it indicates potential economic imbalances, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of cases when PAYEMS growth is above 0.5% and RSAFS growth is below 0.5%, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of cases when GDPC1 is high, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 210 indicates inflationary pressures, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of cases when CPIAUCSL is above 210, this hypothesis is falsified.
